SECTION_TITLE: The Mechanical Core: Sliding Windows, BDP Pipelining, and Retransmission Stalls
SECTION_BODY:
Now let us resolve the throughput dilemma from Section 1: How does a transport protocol send data across high-latency links without collapsing, and what price does that reliability extract?

Sliding Window Mechanics & The Bandwidth-Delay Product

Instead of Stop-and-Wait, TCP uses pipelining. The sender is allowed to transmit a continuous stream of packets onto the wire without waiting for an immediate acknowledgment, up to a maximum allowed limit called the Window.

The volume of data that can physically inhabit the fiber optical cable at any instant is governed by the Bandwidth-Delay Product (BDP)💡 Bandwidth-Delay Product (BDP)Network Capacity MetricThe physical capacity of a network path, calculated as Bandwidth × RTT. It represents the maximum volume of unacknowledged data that can be in flight simultaneously without starving the link or overflowing intermediate buffers.. On a 10 Gbps fiber line between New York and London with 60 ms RTT, the physical math is explicit:

BDP = Bandwidth × RTT
BDP = (10,000,000,000 bits/sec ÷ 8) × 0.060 sec = 1,250 MB/s × 0.060 sec = 75 Megabytes (75 MB)

This physical reality means the fiber optic cable can hold 75 MB of in-flight bytes simultaneously. TCP manages how much data is allowed in flight using two complementary variables: the receiver's Receive Window (rwnd)💡 Receive Window (rwnd)Flow ControlThe buffer size advertised back by the receiver in every ACK packet. It prevents a fast sender from overflowing the receiver's available kernel socket memory. and the sender's dynamically estimated Congestion Window (cwnd)💡 Congestion Window (cwnd)Congestion ControlThe sender's internal estimate of how much data the intermediate routers can handle without dropping packets. The sender respects the minimum: Allowed = min(rwnd, cwnd)..

Loss Detection: Cumulative ACKs and Fast Retransmit

When a packet drops in transit, the receiver sends back repeated cumulative acknowledgments for the missing boundary. Upon receiving 3 duplicate ACKs, the sender triggers Fast Retransmit💡 Fast RetransmitLoss RecoveryAn algorithmic loss detection mechanism where a TCP sender immediately retransmits a missing segment after receiving 3 duplicate acknowledgments, without waiting for the expiration of the slower Retransmission Timeout (RTO) timer., paying exactly 1 round-trip of Head-of-Line stall penalty.
